independence_caveat: A reviewer with no access to the producing reasoning. It was given the two card anchors and a rubric only, and was barred from the adjudication record, the manifests, this record and the commit history. It was told to verify against issuing-body text and never by finding a second site that repeats a claim.
scope: The 2 new cards of batch G2, both created from the fifth candidate submission.
outcome: Both cards required fixes. 17 edits applied. Neither card was left live with a known defect.

cards.verdict_basis: PASS after all seven independent findings were fixed.
authority_checked: Vessel identity: Panama flag, Panamax bulk carrier, built 1998, 225 m x 32.26 m.
Cargo about 72,100 t iron ore fines, loaded Paradip.
24 crew, 2 rescued from liferafts by a passing tanker, 22 missing.
Cause undetermined and no investigation report published.
Casualty Investigation Code Res. MSC.255(84), mandatory via SOLAS Ch. XI-1, non-punitive - checked against the Code text itself.
IMSBC 7-day moisture sampling rule, re-test after rain, the can test, and carriage above TML only in a specially constructed or fitted ship.
SOLAS Ch. XII additional measures for bulk carriers including hold water-level detectors.

findings_fixed.severity: the one that had to be fixed before a candidate saw it
findings_fixed.defect: The card stated flatly, in three places, that TML is 90% of the Flow Moisture Point - and in an adjacent bullet said iron ore fines uses the modified Proctor/Fagerberg test. Those two statements are mutually exclusive. For IRON ORE FINES, the cargo this whole card is about, TML is the critical moisture content at 80% degree of saturation and there is NO FMP. A candidate reciting 'TML is 90% of FMP' and then asked 'and for iron ore fines?' is caught.
findings_fixed.fix: All three places now state which test route gives which TML, and that iron ore fines has no FMP. The Common CE Failures entry was rewritten so the trap itself becomes the lesson.

findings_fixed.defect: Group A was defined as cargoes that 'may liquefy'. Since the 05-19/06-21 amendments the definition is 'may liquefy OR UNDERGO DYNAMIC SEPARATION'.
findings_fixed.fix: Full definition restored in both places, with a note that 'define Group A' is where the examiner chain starts.

findings_fixed.defect: The Casualty Investigation Code constructs were conflated. Panama was called 'the substantially interested State with primary responsibility'; it is the MARINE SAFETY INVESTIGATING State. And the Indian interest was grounded on the cargo loading at its port and its assets running the search - neither of which is a limb of the definition.
findings_fixed.fix: Rewritten to name the correct constructs, to ground the Indian interest on being the coastal State involved, and to note that at that distance the casualty is on the HIGH SEAS.

findings_fixed.defect: The sinking date was asserted as 22 August. Sources conflict between 21 and 22 August, including the Indian Director General of Shipping.
findings_fixed.fix: Stem and body now read '21 or 22 August', and the hedge was widened to name the date as disputed.

findings_fixed.defect: Time to sink given as 'under ten minutes'. The figure attributed to the Director General of Shipping from the survivor account is about eight minutes.
findings_fixed.fix: Now 'about eight minutes', noting some reports say under ten.

findings_fixed.defect: Distance given as 240 nm; reports range 230-240 nm and one places her considerably further east.
findings_fixed.fix: Now '230 to 240 nautical miles' with the spread acknowledged.

findings_fixed.defect: 'the MRCC with the Indian Coast Guard and Indian Navy' reads as three bodies; the MRCC is a Coast Guard facility.
findings_fixed.fix: Now 'the Indian Coast Guard MRCC with Indian Navy assets'.

cards.explicitly_confirmed_sound: The reviewer read the card in full for the thing that mattered most and confirmed it: the cause is NEVER asserted as fact - the 15-second, the 60-second, section 1, the reference-box status line, the trap question and the Common CE Failures entry all state it is hypothesis. It called the handling of an open casualty with 22 missing seafarers exemplary, and the liquefaction engineering sound.
cards.not_stated: Crew nationalities were deliberately NOT added to the card: the two independent reviews returned different splits (18 versus 20 Chinese nationals), and a disputed number about people who are missing is not something to print.

cards.verdict_basis: PASS after all four independent findings were fixed.
authority_checked: LNG boiling point about -162 C; expansion about 600:1; methane flammable 5-15% by volume; auto-ignition about 537 C.
ESD1 stops transfer and closes valves, ESD2 operates the emergency release coupling.
Dry chemical powder as the primary medium; do not extinguish a gas fire you cannot isolate; water never into the pool but yes for boundary cooling and vapour dispersion.
Cryogenic embrittlement and rapid phase transition.
IGF Code for gas-FUELLED ships through SOLAS Ch. II-1 Part G; IGC Code for gas CARRIERS; SIGTTO and SGMF as industry guidance rather than statute.

findings_fixed.defect: 'Auto-ignition about 537 C, which is high - methane is hard to ignite'. A high auto-ignition temperature means it resists a HOT SURFACE. The minimum ignition energy is about 0.28 mJ, so a spark or static discharge ignites it instantly. 'Hard to ignite' invites the examiner to ask why you control ignition sources at all - and the candidate has already conceded the point.
findings_fixed.fix: Rewritten to give both figures and to say the working precaution is ignition-source control, not surface temperature.

findings_fixed.defect: 'stratified cargoes' on a gas-FUELLED ship, in a card that had just insisted on the IGC/IGF cargo-versus-fuel distinction.
findings_fixed.fix: Rewritten as fuel, with the rollover mechanism stated properly.

findings_fixed.defect: The card said what ESD1 and ESD2 DO but never what initiates them - and its own deep-dive stresses that the ESD must be tested rather than assumed.
findings_fixed.fix: Added the trigger set: gas detection, low-temperature alarm in the drip tray, tank level and pressure, fire detection, loss of the ship-shore link or excessive movement, plus manual initiation from both sides.
Now stated at atmospheric pressure and ambient temperature.

cards.explicitly_confirmed_sound: The reviewer singled out the minor/major dividing line - can I isolate the source? - as correctly drawn, and the sentence about an extinguished leak that is still leaking producing an unignited flammable cloud as the highest-value line on the card.

batch_level_findings: Neither card names an examiner. AUG-0050 is individually attributed to Senthil by its candidate, but that evidence is recorded in the intake store rather than injected into the examiner index through card markup, so relationships stay at 958.

Both cards are two-occurrence cards and neither merge was made by the parser: AUG-0044 into AUG-0042, and AUG-0050 corroborating AUG-0035. Both merges are recorded in the adjudication where they can be reviewed.

The reviewer judgement on QB2_A#q31 is worth keeping as a standard: on an OPEN casualty the mechanism may be taught but the cause may not be asserted, and the tone must acknowledge the people still missing.
